findings.evidence: Branch detection uses `git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/<arg>"` or `refs/remotes/<arg>`. For a valid fully qualified argument such as `refs/remotes/origin/feature/x`, both probes prepend another refs prefix and fail. The argument consequently falls through to rule 7's single-commit explanation instead of the branch changeset.
findings.fix: Handle arguments already starting with refs/heads/ or refs/remotes/ by verifying that exact ref with `git show-ref --verify --quiet "$arg"` before attempting the shorthand probes. Route confirmed branch refs through rule 6 and preserve the remote-base preference for refs/remotes/ arguments.

findings.evidence: The large-PR branch says to run `gh pr diff "<pr>" --color=never > "$(mktemp)"` and then read the saved patch in sections. The temporary pathname is neither retained nor printed, so the next read has no known path.
findings.fix: Retain and expose the pathname, for example `patch=$(mktemp) && gh pr diff "<pr>" --color=never > "$patch" && printf '%s\n' "$patch"`. Check the command's status and use the printed absolute path for subsequent section reads.
